decisions.choice: los que no conocen a Dios (B); la gente que no conoce a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The usual Readable wording for this word, "los que no son judíos", does not fit here: the readers were mostly Gentiles themselves, and the meaning decision reads the word as the unbelieving world around them.

decisions.choice: watu wasiomjua Mungu
decisions.reason: The usual Readable wording for this word, "watu wasio Wayahudi", does not fit here: the readers were mostly Gentiles themselves, and the meaning decision reads the word as the unbelieving world around them.

decisions.choice: les nations (L)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians, "les nations" keeps the biblical sense of the peoples who do not know God (meaning decision m2); "les païens" would sound pejorative. Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: "이방 사람들" (L); "하나님을 모르는 사람들" (B, R); "영광을 돌리다" for glorify
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of Romans: "이방 사람" is understood, and here the meaning decision reads it as people who do not know God, which Balanced and Readable say, as the English does. "영광을 돌리다" is the current Korean for glorifying God, as in the Korean Romans 1:21.

decisions.choice: "các dân ngoại" (L) for the Gentiles
decisions.reason: The Gentiles here are people who do not know God (m2), not simply non-Jews, since the readers themselves are mostly Gentiles. Literal keeps the church word, as the Vietnamese Romans does; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

source.text: Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν κύριον· εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι, εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς δι’ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν·

records.literal_gloss: Be subject to every human institution because of the Lord; whether to king as being supreme, \v 14 or to governors as through him being sent for punishment of evildoers and praise of those doing good; \v 15 because thus is the will of the God, doing good to muzzle the of the foolish men ignorance;

en.L: Be subject to every human institution for the sake of the Lord, whether to [the] king as being supreme, \v 14 or to governors as sent by him for punishment of evildoers and praise of those who do good; \v 15 because so is the will of God, [that] by doing good [you] silence the ignorance of foolish {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: For the Lord's sake, place yourselves under every authority that people have set up: the emperor, who holds the highest rank, \v 14 and the governors he sends out to punish wrongdoing and to reward good conduct with praise. \v 15 For this is God's will: that by doing good you muzzle the ignorance of foolish {{gender:people|men}}.
en.R: Because you belong to the Lord, respect every human authority and accept its rule. Respect the emperor, because he is the highest ruler. \v 14 Respect the governors too. The emperor sends them to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right. \v 15 God wants you to do good. When you do, foolish {{gender:people|men}} who talk about you without knowing what they are saying will have nothing more to say.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sométanse|Someteos}} a toda institución humana por causa del Señor; sea al rey, como el que está por encima, \v 14 sea a [los] gobernadores, como enviados por él para castigar a los malhechores y alabar a los que hacen el bien; \v 15 porque así es la voluntad de Dios: [que] haciendo el bien {{plural_you:silencien|silenciéis}} la ignorancia de {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}}.
es.B: Por amor al Señor, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} bajo toda autoridad que los seres humanos han establecido: el emperador, que ocupa el rango más alto, \v 14 y los gobernadores que él envía para castigar el mal y premiar con elogios la buena conducta. \v 15 Porque esta es la voluntad de Dios: que, haciendo el bien, {{plural_you:silencien|silenciéis}} la ignorancia de {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}}.
es.R: Porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} al Señor, {{plural_you:respeten|respetad}} a toda autoridad humana y {{plural_you:acepten|aceptad}} su gobierno. {{plural_you:Respeten|Respetad}} al emperador, porque es el gobernante más alto. \v 14 {{plural_you:Respeten|Respetad}} también a los gobernadores. El emperador los envía para castigar a los que hacen el mal y para alabar a los que hacen el bien. \v 15 Dios quiere que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} el bien. Cuando lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}} que hablan de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin saber lo que dicen ya no tendrán nada que decir.

sw.L: Nyenyekeeni kila mamlaka ya kibinadamu kwa ajili ya Bwana; ikiwa ni mfalme, kama aliye mkuu kuliko wote, \v 14 au watawala, kama waliotumwa naye kwa ajili ya kuwaadhibu watenda maovu na kuwasifu watenda mema; \v 15 kwa sababu ndivyo yalivyo mapenzi ya Mungu, [kwamba] kwa kutenda mema mnyamazishe ujinga wa watu wapumbavu.
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya Bwana, nyenyekeeni kila mamlaka iliyowekwa na wanadamu: Kaisari, aliye na cheo cha juu kuliko wote, \v 14 na watawala anaowatuma kuadhibu maovu na kusifu mwenendo mwema. \v 15 Kwa maana haya ndiyo mapenzi ya Mungu: kwamba kwa kutenda mema mnyamazishe ujinga wa watu wapumbavu.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa ninyi ni wa Bwana, heshimuni kila mamlaka ya kibinadamu na mkubali utawala wake. Mheshimuni Kaisari, kwa sababu yeye ndiye mtawala mkuu kuliko wote. \v 14 Waheshimuni pia watawala. Kaisari huwatuma ili wawaadhibu wale wanaotenda mabaya na kuwasifu wale wanaotenda mema. \v 15 Mungu anataka mtende mema. Mnapofanya hivyo, watu wapumbavu wanaowasema bila kujua wanachosema watakosa la kusema.

fr.L: Soumettez-vous à toute institution humaine à cause du Seigneur, soit au roi comme souverain, \v 14 soit aux gouverneurs comme envoyés par lui pour punir les malfaiteurs et louer ceux qui font le bien ; \v 15 car telle est la volonté de Dieu, [qu’]en faisant le bien [vous] museliez l’ignorance {{gender:des gens insensés|des hommes insensés}}.
fr.B: À cause du Seigneur, soumettez-vous à toute autorité établie parmi les humains : à l’empereur, qui a le rang le plus élevé, \v 14 et aux gouverneurs qu’il envoie pour punir ceux qui font le mal et récompenser par des éloges ceux qui font le bien. \v 15 Car voici la volonté de Dieu : qu’en faisant le bien, vous réduisiez au silence l’ignorance {{gender:des gens insensés|des hommes insensés}}.
fr.R: Parce que vous appartenez au Seigneur, respectez toute autorité humaine et acceptez son pouvoir. Respectez l’empereur, parce que c’est le plus haut chef. \v 14 Respectez aussi les gouverneurs. L’empereur les envoie pour punir ceux qui font le mal et pour féliciter ceux qui font le bien. \v 15 Dieu veut que vous fassiez le bien. Quand vous le faites, {{gender:les gens insensés|les hommes insensés}} qui parlent de vous sans savoir ce qu’ils disent n’ont plus rien à dire.

ko.L: 주님을 위하여 사람이 세운 모든 제도에 복종하십시오. 최고 권위를 가진 왕에게나, \v 14 악을 행하는 사람들을 벌하고 선을 행하는 사람들을 칭찬하라고 그가 보낸 총독들에게나 [복종하십시오]. \v 15 선을 행함으로 어리석은 사람들의 무지한 [말을] 막는 것이 하나님의 뜻이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 주님을 위해, 사람들이 세운 모든 권위 아래 자신을 두십시오. 가장 높은 자리에 있는 황제에게나, \v 14 악한 일을 벌하고 선한 일을 칭찬하라고 황제가 보낸 총독들에게나 그렇게 하십시오. \v 15 선을 행하여 어리석은 사람들의 무지한 입을 막는 것, 이것이 하나님의 뜻입니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 주님께 속한 사람들이니, 사람이 세운 모든 권위를 존중하고 그 다스림을 받아들이십시오. 황제는 가장 높은 통치자이니 황제를 존중하십시오. \v 14 총독들도 존중하십시오. 황제는 나쁜 일을 하는 사람들을 벌하고 옳은 일을 하는 사람들을 칭찬하라고 그들을 보냅니다. \v 15 하나님께서는 여러분이 선한 일을 하기를 원하십니다. 그러면 무엇을 말하는지도 모르고 여러분에 대해 떠드는 어리석은 사람들이 더 할 말이 없게 될 것입니다.

vi.L: Hãy thuận phục mọi thể chế của loài người vì cớ Chúa, hoặc vua là đấng tối cao, \v 14 hoặc các quan tổng đốc là những người được vua sai đến để trừng phạt kẻ làm ác và khen ngợi người làm lành; \v 15 vì ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời là như vậy: [anh chị em] bởi làm lành mà bịt miệng sự ngu dốt của những người dại dột.
vi.B: Vì cớ Chúa, hãy thuận phục mọi thẩm quyền do loài người lập ra: hoàng đế, là người giữ địa vị cao nhất, \v 14 và các quan tổng đốc được hoàng đế sai đến để trừng phạt việc làm ác và khen thưởng việc làm lành. \v 15 Vì ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời là như thế này: anh chị em làm điều lành để bịt miệng sự ngu dốt của những người dại dột.
vi.R: Vì anh chị em thuộc về Chúa, hãy tôn trọng mọi thẩm quyền của loài người và chấp nhận sự cai trị của họ. Hãy tôn trọng hoàng đế, vì ông là người cai trị cao nhất. \v 14 Cũng hãy tôn trọng các quan tổng đốc. Hoàng đế sai họ đi để trừng phạt những kẻ làm sai và khen ngợi những người làm đúng. \v 15 Đức Chúa Trời muốn anh chị em làm điều tốt. Khi anh chị em làm như vậy, những người dại dột nói về anh chị em mà không biết mình đang nói gì sẽ chẳng còn gì để nói nữa.

pt.L: Submetam-se a toda instituição humana por causa do Senhor, seja ao rei, como soberano, \v 14 seja a governadores, como enviados por ele para castigo dos malfeitores e louvor dos que fazem o bem; \v 15 porque assim é a vontade de Deus, [que], fazendo o bem, [vocês] façam calar a ignorância {{gender:das pessoas insensatas|dos homens insensatos}}.
pt.B: Por causa do Senhor, submetam-se a toda autoridade que as pessoas instituíram: ao imperador, que ocupa a posição mais alta, \v 14 e aos governadores que ele envia para castigar quem faz o mal e para recompensar com elogios quem faz o bem. \v 15 Pois esta é a vontade de Deus: que, fazendo o bem, vocês tapem a boca da ignorância {{gender:das pessoas insensatas|dos homens insensatos}}.
pt.R: Porque vocês pertencem ao Senhor, respeitem toda autoridade humana e aceitem o seu governo. Respeitem o imperador, porque ele é o governante mais alto. \v 14 Respeitem também os governadores. O imperador os envia para castigar quem faz o mal e para elogiar quem faz o bem. \v 15 Deus quer que vocês façam o bem. Quando vocês fazem isso, {{gender:as pessoas tolas|os homens tolos}} que falam de vocês sem saber o que estão dizendo não vão ter mais nada a dizer.

decisions.choice: be subject: accept your place under their authority
decisions.reason: Ὑποτάγητε means to place oneself under someone in an order. It asks for respect and cooperation, not for doing whatever is commanded: the same letter tells believers to fear God (verse 17) and not to fear what others fear (3:14), and the apostles refused an order to stop preaching (Acts 5:29).

decisions.choice: every human institution: every authority set up among people
alternatives: every human creature: every human being
decisions.reason: κτίσει normally means creation or a creature, so the phrase could mean "every human being" (compare "honor everyone" in verse 17). But the examples that follow are the emperor and governors, and the word was also used of something established or founded. So it is read here as human authorities.

decisions.choice: for the Lord's sake: because of Christ
decisions.reason: κύριον is Christ, as in 2:3 and 3:15. Believers accept human authority because of their loyalty to him and so that his name is not slandered (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the king: the Roman emperor
decisions.reason: βασιλεῖ was the ordinary Greek title for the Roman emperor in the eastern provinces. He ruled over all the provinces Peter writes to (1:1); governors were his appointed officials there.

decisions.choice: sent by him: sent by the emperor
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to the king just named. Governors in the provinces held power from the emperor. That God stands behind all such authority is said elsewhere (Romans 13:1), not here.

decisions.choice: this is God's will: that by doing good you silence ignorant people
alternatives: this is God's will, as just said; doing good, you silence them
decisions.reason: οὕτως points forward to the participle and infinitive that follow. God wants his people to answer slander by doing good.

decisions.choice: to silence: to muzzle
decisions.reason: φιμοῦν means to muzzle an animal, and then to silence someone. Good conduct leaves the accusers with nothing to say.

decisions.choice: the emperor
decisions.reason: In English "the king" suggests a monarch of one nation; the person meant was the Roman emperor (m4). Literal keeps "king".

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings; "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: Because you belong to the Lord
alternatives: for the sake of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says why "for the Lord's sake" matters to the readers (m3).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Sométanse|Someteos}}
decisions.reason: "Someterse" is used for this verb here, for household servants in verse 18 and for wives in 3:1, so Literal shows that one verb runs through the household instructions.

decisions.choice: nyenyekeeni
decisions.reason: "Kunyenyekea" (to submit, place oneself under) is used for this verb here, for household servants in verse 18 and for wives in 3:1, as in Ephesians 5. "Kutii" (obey) would say more than the meaning decision allows.

decisions.choice: Kaisari
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Roman emperor (meaning decision on the king). "Kaisari" is the title Swahili readers know from the Gospels for the emperor in Rome; Literal keeps "mfalme".

decisions.choice: soumettez-vous
decisions.reason: As in Colossians, the reflexive says that the readers place themselves under authority by their own choice (meaning decision m1); "soyez soumis" would describe a state imposed on them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:des gens insensés|des hommes insensés}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women; "gens" is the inclusive default and "hommes" the traditional alternative. The adjective has the same form after both nouns.
The king is the Roman emperor (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek word, and Balanced and Readable say who he was, as the English does. The same in 2:17.

decisions.choice: "사람이 세운 모든 제도" (L); "사람들이 세운 모든 권위" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as every authority set up among people, and footnotes the reading "every human creature". Literal keeps "제도" (institution), close to the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "권위", which the next clauses name.

decisions.choice: "vua" (L); "hoàng đế" (B, R) for the king, the Roman emperor (also 2:17)
decisions.reason: The king meant is the Roman emperor (m4). Literal keeps Peter's word; Balanced and Readable say "hoàng đế", as the English says "the emperor". The pronouns for him are ordinary: "vua", "ông", with no capital.

decisions.choice: "thuận phục" (L, B) for be subject (also 2:18; 3:1)
decisions.reason: To be subject is to accept one's place under an authority (m1). "Thuận phục" is the word the Vietnamese Colossians and Romans use for this verb (Colossians 3:18; Romans 13:1); "vâng phục" is kept for obedience.

decisions.choice: {{gender:das pessoas insensatas|dos homens insensatos}} (L, B); {{gender:as pessoas tolas|os homens tolos}} (R)
decisions.reason: The adjective agrees with the noun the setting chooses, so it goes inside both options. "Insensato" at Literal and Balanced, "tolo" at Readable, the book's words for a fool.

source.text: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν, ἀλλ’ ὡς θεοῦ δοῦλοι.

records.literal_gloss: as free, and not as a covering having of the evil the freedom, but as of God slaves.

en.L: [Live] as free {{gender:people|men}}, and not as [those] having freedom as a covering for evil, but as slaves of God.
en.B: Act as free {{gender:people|men}}. Your freedom is not a mask for wickedness; you are slaves who belong to God.
en.R: You are free. But do not use your freedom as an excuse to do wrong. Live as God's slaves, people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}}] como {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}, y no como [quienes] tienen la libertad como cubierta de la maldad, sino como esclavos de Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Actúen|Actuad}} como {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} libertad no es una máscara para la maldad; {{plural_you:son|sois}} esclavos que pertenecen a Dios.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} libres. Pero no {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} libertad como excusa para hacer el mal. {{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}} como esclavos de Dios, personas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pertenecen.

sw.L: [Ishini] kama watu huru, wala si kama [wale] walio na uhuru kama kifuniko cha uovu, bali kama watumwa wa Mungu.
sw.B: Enendeni kama watu huru. Uhuru wenu si kinyago cha kuficha uovu; ninyi ni watumwa walio mali ya Mungu.
sw.R: Ninyi ni watu huru. Lakini msitumie uhuru wenu kama sababu ya kutenda mabaya. Ishini kama watumwa wa Mungu, watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

fr.L: [Vivez] comme {{gender:des gens libres|des hommes libres}}, et non comme [ceux qui] ont la liberté comme un voile pour la méchanceté, mais comme des esclaves de Dieu.
fr.B: Agissez en {{gender:gens libres|hommes libres}}. Votre liberté n’est pas un masque pour cacher le mal : vous êtes des esclaves qui appartiennent à Dieu.
fr.R: Vous êtes libres. Mais ne vous servez pas de votre liberté comme d’une excuse pour faire le mal. Vivez comme des esclaves de Dieu, des gens qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartiennent.

ko.L: 자유로운 사람으로서 [사십시오]. 그러나 자유를 악을 가리는 덮개로 삼지 말고, 하나님의 종으로서 [사십시오].
ko.B: 자유로운 사람으로 행동하십시오. 여러분의 자유는 악을 가리는 가면이 아닙니다. 여러분은 하나님께 속한 종입니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 자유롭습니다. 그러나 그 자유를 나쁜 일을 하는 핑계로 삼지 마십시오. 하나님의 종으로, 곧 하나님께 속한 사람으로 사십시오.

vi.L: [Hãy sống] như những người tự do, và đừng như [những người] lấy sự tự do làm màn che cho điều ác, nhưng như những nô lệ của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Hãy sống như những người tự do. Sự tự do của anh chị em không phải là tấm màn che giấu điều ác; anh chị em là những nô lệ thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Anh chị em là người tự do. Nhưng đừng lấy sự tự do làm cớ để làm điều sai trái. Hãy sống như những nô lệ của Đức Chúa Trời, là những người thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: [Vivam] como {{gender:pessoas livres|homens livres}}, e não como [quem] tem a liberdade como cobertura para a maldade, mas como escravos de Deus.
pt.B: Ajam como {{gender:pessoas livres|homens livres}}. A liberdade de vocês não é uma máscara para a maldade; vocês são escravos que pertencem a Deus.
pt.R: Vocês são livres. Mas não usem a liberdade como desculpa para fazer o mal. Vivam como escravos de Deus, pessoas que pertencem a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

decisions.choice: as free people: describes how they are to be subject (verse 13)
decisions.reason: ἐλεύθεροι has no verb of its own. The SBLGNT ends the sentence at verse 15 with a raised dot and at verse 16 with a full stop, so verse 16 continues "be subject": believers submit not as people forced to, but as free people.

decisions.choice: free, yet slaves of God
decisions.reason: Their freedom is real: they have been ransomed from their old way of life (1:18). But it is not freedom to do evil; it is the freedom of people who now belong wholly to God. ἐπικάλυμμα is a covering or veil: freedom must not be used to hide wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: slaves of God: people who belong entirely to God
alternatives: servants of God (in a looser sense)
decisions.reason: δοῦλοι is a slave, someone owned by another. Israel's prophets and leaders were called slaves of God, and believers now are (Romans 6:22; Philippians 1:1). The word stresses belonging and obedience; it points ahead to the household slaves addressed in verse 18.

decisions.choice: [Live] as free
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a verb so the sentence can be read on its own.

decisions.choice: free {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means free persons, men and women; "free men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free, so that the contrast with "free" stays sharp (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}
decisions.reason: The word means free persons, men and women; "hombres libres" is the traditional form, as in the English setting.

decisions.choice: esclavos
decisions.reason: "Esclavo" for this word at every level, as in the English, so that the contrast with "libres" stays sharp. "Siervos" would soften it.

decisions.choice: watumwa
decisions.reason: "Mtumwa" for this word at every level, as in the English, so that the contrast with "huru" stays sharp. "Watumishi" (servants) would soften it.

decisions.choice: esclaves de Dieu (every level)
decisions.reason: Freedom and slavery are set against each other here (meaning decision m2), so, as in the English and the French style guide, "esclaves" is kept at every level: "serviteurs" would lose the paradox of free people who belong entirely to God.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 종" at every level, set against "자유로운 사람"
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide gives "종" at every level; it already says that a person belongs wholly to a master (meaning decision: people who belong entirely to God), and the contrast with "자유" is kept. "노예" is kept for slavery as a social state (2:18).

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level, set against "người tự do"
decisions.reason: Peter sets freedom against slavery to God (m2), so every level keeps "nô lệ", as the English keeps "slaves" under its rule for this word and as the Vietnamese Romans does where slavery and freedom are set side by side (6:6). "Người tự do" needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: escravos de Deus
decisions.reason: For the whole book. "Escravo" at every level here, as the English: the word stands against "livres" (m3), and "servo" would blunt the contrast. The same holds for the household slaves of 2:18.

decisions.choice: the brotherhood: the whole community of believers
decisions.reason: ἀδελφότητα is the family of brothers and sisters in Christ, everywhere in the world (5:9). Love for them is the love of 1:22.

decisions.choice: honor all, including the emperor; fear God alone
decisions.reason: The emperor receives the same honor (τιμᾶτε) as everyone (τιμήσατε); only God is to be feared. The saying recalls Proverbs 24:21 (fear God and the king) but changes it: the king is honored, not feared.

decisions.choice: honor everyone: the heading over the three commands that follow
decisions.reason: The first verb (τιμήσατε) is aorist and the other three are present. Some read the first as a general command that the other three spell out; others read four equal commands. The meaning is little affected.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brotherhood}}
decisions.reason: Inclusive default, as the word means the community of brothers and sisters; "the brotherhood" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: your fellow believers (B); God's family, your fellow believers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the brotherhood is (m1).

decisions.choice: the emperor
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Show respect (R); Have reverence for God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for honor and for the fear of God, which is reverence, not terror.

decisions.choice: la hermandad (L); hermanos (B, R), no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermandad" and "hermanos" already take in brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: udugu (L); ndugu (B, R), no setting
decisions.reason: "Udugu" and "ndugu" already take in brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: aimez {{gender:les frères et sœurs|la fraternité}} (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a collective noun for the community of believers (meaning decision m1). "La fraternité" is its traditional French equivalent but reads as brothers; the inclusive default names the brothers and sisters, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 공동체" (L); "믿음의 식구들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is the whole community of believers as brothers (meaning decision); Literal keeps the family word with the span used for believers, and Balanced and Readable say "the family of faith", which already includes all.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} trong đức tin" (L); "anh chị em cùng đức tin" (B), "cùng niềm tin" (R)
decisions.reason: The brotherhood is the whole community of believers (m1). Literal keeps the family word under the gender setting, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say fellow believers, which in Vietnamese is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: os irmãos na fé
decisions.reason: "Fellow believers" is "os irmãos na fé", as the style guide says for God's people; "os crentes" means Protestants in Brazil. The phrase takes no gender setting: it is the ordinary Portuguese name for the community, which Literal spells out under the setting.

records.literal_gloss: The household slaves, being subject in all fear to the masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.

en.L: Household slaves, [be] subject with all fear to [your] masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.
en.B: Household slaves, place yourselves under your masters with deep reverence, not just those who are kind and gentle but also those who are crooked and harsh.
en.R: You who are slaves in a household, respect your masters and accept their authority. Do this out of reverence for God. Do it whether your masters are kind and gentle or cruel and unfair.

es.L: Criados, [{{plural_you:estén|estad}}] sometidos con todo temor a [{{plural_you:sus|vuestros}}] amos, no solo a los buenos y amables, sino también a los torcidos.
es.B: Criados, {{plural_you:sométanse|someteos}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos con profunda reverencia, no solo a los que son buenos y comprensivos, sino también a los que son injustos y duros.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} como criados en una casa, {{plural_you:respeten|respetad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos y {{plural_you:acepten|aceptad}} su autoridad. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} por reverencia a Dios. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} tanto si {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos son buenos y amables como si son crueles e injustos.

sw.L: Watumishi wa nyumbani, [muwe] mkiwanyenyekea mabwana [wenu] kwa hofu yote, si kwa walio wema na wenye upole peke yao, bali pia kwa walio wapotovu.

fr.L: Esclaves de maison, [soyez] soumis avec toute crainte à [vos] maîtres, non seulement à ceux qui sont bons et doux, mais aussi aux [maîtres] tortueux.
fr.B: Esclaves de maison, soumettez-vous à vos maîtres avec un profond respect, non seulement à ceux qui sont bons et doux, mais aussi à ceux qui sont injustes et durs.
fr.R: Vous qui êtes esclaves dans une maison, respectez vos maîtres et acceptez leur autorité. Faites-le par respect pour Dieu. Faites-le, que vos maîtres soient bons et doux ou cruels et injustes.

ko.L: 집안 노예 여러분, 모든 두려움으로 주인들에게 복종하십시오. 선하고 너그러운 주인들에게뿐 아니라 비뚤어진 주인들에게도 [그렇게 하십시오].
ko.B: 집안에서 일하는 노예 여러분, 깊이 두려워하는 마음으로 주인들의 권위 아래 자신을 두십시오. 선하고 너그러운 주인들에게뿐 아니라 비뚤어지고 가혹한 주인들에게도 그렇게 하십시오.
ko.R: 한 집안의 노예로 있는 여러분, 주인을 존중하고 그 권위를 받아들이십시오. 하나님을 두려워하는 마음으로 그렇게 하십시오. 주인이 친절하고 너그럽든지, 잔인하고 불공평하든지 그렇게 하십시오.

vi.L: Hỡi những người làm nô lệ trong nhà, hãy thuận phục chủ mình với tất cả lòng kính sợ, không chỉ với những chủ tốt và hiền hòa, mà cả với những chủ khó tính.
vi.B: Hỡi những người làm nô lệ trong nhà, hãy hết lòng kính sợ mà thuận phục chủ mình, không chỉ những chủ tốt và hiền hòa, mà cả những chủ ngang ngược và khắc nghiệt.
vi.R: Anh chị em là những người làm nô lệ trong một gia đình, hãy tôn trọng chủ mình và chấp nhận quyền của họ. Hãy làm điều đó vì lòng kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời. Hãy làm như vậy dù chủ mình tử tế và hiền hòa hay độc ác và bất công.

pt.L: Escravos domésticos, [sejam] submissos com todo temor aos [seus] senhores, não somente aos bons e gentis, mas também aos perversos.
pt.B: Escravos domésticos, submetam-se aos seus senhores com profunda reverência, não apenas aos que são bons e gentis, mas também aos que são perversos e duros.
pt.R: Vocês que são escravos numa casa, respeitem os seus senhores e aceitem a autoridade deles. Façam isso por reverência a Deus. Façam isso quer os seus senhores sejam bons e gentis, quer sejam cruéis e injustos.

decisions.choice: household slaves in the Roman world; what the letter does and does not address
decisions.reason: Many households included slaves, who were their owners' legal property and could be beaten (verse 20). Some held responsible posts; others did hard labor. Many were later freed. Peter speaks to believing slaves, many of whom had masters who did not share their faith and could be cruel. Unlike Colossians 3:22-4:1 and Ephesians 6:5-9, he gives no word to masters. The letter does not discuss whether slavery should exist. It tells slaves how to live under unjust treatment as people who belong to God (verse 16) and follow Christ's example (verses 21-25). It does not say that their suffering is deserved or that God approves of cruelty.

decisions.choice: household slaves
decisions.reason: οἰκέται is a different word from δοῦλος. It means a member of a household's staff, and in practice nearly always a slave who worked in the house. The word is chosen for the household setting, not to describe a freer status: these people could be struck by their owners (verse 20). The owners are δεσπόταις, a word for absolute owners and masters.

decisions.choice: be subject: a participle used as a command
decisions.reason: ὑποτασσόμενοι is a participle with no main verb; as often in household instructions, it gives a command. It applies to slaves the same verb as verse 13 (be subject).

decisions.choice: with all fear: reverence for God
decisions.reason: In 1 Peter the one to be feared is God (1:17; 2:17), and believers are told not to fear people (3:6, 3:14). So φόβῳ here most likely means reverence for God, which shapes how slaves act toward their masters.

decisions.choice: the crooked: harsh, unjust masters
decisions.reason: σκολιοῖς means bent or crooked, and then perverse or unfair. The contrast is with masters who are good and ἐπιεικέσιν (gentle, reasonable).

decisions.choice: household slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: Peter speaks to household slaves as a social class, people actually owned, next to their "masters" (m1, m2), and "servant" would change the meaning for modern readers (style guide). "Household" keeps what this word adds. "Servants" would suggest free people working for pay.

decisions.choice: out of reverence for God
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the fear is for (m4).

decisions.choice: criados
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:4, "criado" is kept for this word, a member of a household's staff, so that it stays distinct from "esclavo" (verse 16) and "servidor". The meaning decision says these people were in practice slaves who could be beaten (verse 20), which the English makes explicit with "household slaves"; a reviewer may prefer "esclavos domésticos".

decisions.choice: watumishi wa nyumbani
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:4, "mtumishi wa nyumbani" is kept for this word, a member of a household's staff, so that it stays distinct from "mtumwa" (verse 16) and "mtumishi". The meaning decision says these people were in practice slaves who could be beaten (verse 20), which the English makes explicit with "household slaves"; a reviewer may prefer "watumwa wa nyumbani".

decisions.choice: Esclaves de maison (L, B); esclaves dans une maison (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, the people addressed were owned, not hired (meaning decisions m1 and m2), and their situation as slaves is the point of verses 18-20. French "domestiques" would suggest paid household staff.

decisions.choice: "집안 노예 여러분" (L); "집안에서 일하는 노예 여러분" (B); "한 집안의 노예로 있는 여러분" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is household slaves in the Roman world (meaning decision), so every level keeps the hard word "노예", as the English keeps "slaves" and the Korean Colossians 3:22 says "노예 여러분": slavery itself is the point here. "여러분" keeps the letter's respectful address for every group.

decisions.choice: "những người làm nô lệ trong nhà" at every level
decisions.reason: The word is household slaves, people owned by the household they served (m1, m2), and the English keeps "household slaves" at every level. Vietnamese keeps "nô lệ", with the household named, and the respectful "những người làm" that the Vietnamese Colossians uses for the households it addresses (3:18-22).

decisions.choice: escravos domésticos; senhores
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): "escravo" at every level, since these were people owned by their masters (m1, m2); "servos" and "criados" would make them sound like hired staff, and "empregados domésticos" names a modern job. "Senhores", lowercase, is the usual word for a slave's masters.

source.text: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως·

records.literal_gloss: This for [is] grace, if because of consciousness of God endures someone griefs, suffering unjustly;

en.L: For this [is] grace, if, because of awareness of God, someone endures griefs, suffering unjustly.
en.B: For this finds favor: when someone, mindful of God, bears up under pain while suffering unjustly.
en.R: God is pleased when someone suffers unfairly and bears the pain because {{gender:they keep|he keeps}} God in mind.

es.L: Porque esto [es] gracia, si, a causa de [la] conciencia de Dios, alguien soporta penas, sufriendo injustamente.
es.B: Porque esto halla favor: que alguien, consciente de Dios, soporte el dolor cuando sufre injustamente.
es.R: Dios se agrada cuando alguien sufre injustamente y soporta el dolor porque tiene presente a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana hii [ni] neema, ikiwa, kwa sababu ya kumtambua Mungu, mtu anastahimili huzuni, akiteswa kwa udhalimu.
sw.B: Kwa maana hili linapata kibali: mtu anapovumilia maumivu akiteswa kwa udhalimu, kwa kuwa anamkumbuka Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu anapendezwa mtu anapoteswa bila kosa na kuvumilia maumivu kwa sababu anamweka Mungu akilini.

fr.L: Car c’est une grâce si, à cause de [la] conscience de Dieu, quelqu’un supporte des peines en souffrant injustement.
fr.B: Car voici ce qui trouve faveur : que quelqu’un, attentif à Dieu, supporte la douleur en souffrant injustement.
fr.R: Dieu est content quand quelqu’un souffre injustement et supporte la douleur parce qu’il pense à Dieu.

ko.L: 누가 하나님을 의식하기 때문에 부당하게 고난을 받으면서 슬픔을 견딘다면, 이것은 은혜입니다.
ko.B: 누구든지 하나님을 생각하며, 부당하게 고난을 받으면서도 그 아픔을 참는다면, 그것은 하나님께서 기뻐하시는 일입니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 부당하게 고난을 받으면서도 하나님을 생각하여 그 아픔을 참는다면, 하나님께서 그것을 기뻐하십니다.

vi.L: Vì đây là ân điển: nếu vì ý thức về Đức Chúa Trời mà một người chịu đựng những nỗi đau, chịu khổ cách bất công.
vi.B: Vì điều này được Đức Chúa Trời đẹp lòng: khi một người, vì nghĩ đến Đức Chúa Trời, chịu đựng đau đớn trong khi phải chịu khổ cách bất công.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời hài lòng khi một người phải chịu khổ cách bất công mà vẫn chịu đựng nỗi đau, vì người ấy luôn nghĩ đến Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: Pois isto [é] graça, se, por consciência de Deus, alguém suporta tristezas, sofrendo injustamente.
pt.B: Pois isto conta com o favor de Deus: quando alguém, consciente de Deus, suporta dores sofrendo injustamente.
pt.R: Deus se agrada quando alguém sofre injustamente e suporta a dor porque pensa em Deus.

decisions.choice: grace here: what finds favor with God
decisions.reason: χάρις here does not mean God's gift of salvation but something that wins favor, as verse 20 shows: "this is χάρις with God" (compare Luke 6:32-34, where the word means credit or thanks). Enduring unjust suffering for God's sake is what God looks on with favor. The word is still the letter's word for grace (1:2, 5:12), and that link may be intended.

decisions.choice: awareness of God: because one is mindful of God
decisions.reason: συνείδησιν with θεοῦ is consciousness of God: the slave bears unjust treatment because he or she knows God sees and keeps faith with God.

decisions.choice: someone: any believer, though slaves are addressed
decisions.reason: τις makes a general statement. It applies first to the slaves of verse 18, but the same holds for any believer who suffers unjustly (3:14, 3:17; 4:14-16).

decisions.choice: this finds favor (B); God is pleased (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense (m1). Literal keeps the word "grace" so that the reader sees it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they keep|he keeps}}
decisions.reason: Singular "they" for someone; "he" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: quelqu’un ... parce qu’il pense à Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable needs a gender span for its pronoun. In French, "quelqu’un" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no span is needed (French style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "은혜" (L); "하나님께서 기뻐하시는 일" (B, R), here and in verse 20
decisions.reason: The key term for grace is used here of what finds favor with God (meaning decision), as the English Balanced says "finds favor". Literal keeps "은혜" so the word can be traced; Balanced and Readable say what it means, since "은혜" in Korean is only what God gives.

decisions.choice: "ân điển" (L); "được Đức Chúa Trời đẹp lòng" (B), "Đức Chúa Trời hài lòng" (R) (also 2:20)
decisions.reason: Here the word for grace means what finds favour with God (m1). Literal keeps the key term so the reader sees Peter's word; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
alternatives: a gender span on a supplied pronoun
decisions.reason: The English Readable needs a pronoun for "someone" and puts it under the gender setting. Portuguese "alguém" with a verb needs no pronoun and is already inclusive (style section 7), so there is no span.

source.text: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: What kind for credit [is it] if sinning and being struck you will endure?

en.L: For what credit [is it] if, when you sin and are struck, you endure [it]?
en.B: For what is praiseworthy about putting up with blows when you have done wrong?
en.R: If you are beaten because you did wrong, and you put up with it, you deserve no praise for that.

es.L: Porque ¿qué mérito [hay] si, cuando {{plural_you:pecan|pecáis}} y {{plural_you:son|sois}} abofeteados, lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}?
es.B: Porque ¿qué tiene de admirable soportar golpes cuando {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho el mal?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:los|os}} golpean porque {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} algo malo, y lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, no {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}} ningún elogio por ello.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni sifa gani ikiwa, mkitenda dhambi na kupigwa ngumi, mtastahimili?
sw.B: Kwa maana kuna fahari gani kuvumilia mapigo mkiwa mmetenda mabaya?
sw.R: Mkipigwa kwa sababu mlitenda mabaya, nanyi mkavumilia, hamstahili kusifiwa kwa hilo.

fr.L: Car quelle gloire [y a-t-il] si, quand vous péchez et êtes frappés, vous [le] supportez ?
fr.B: Car quel mérite y a-t-il à supporter les coups quand vous avez mal agi ?
fr.R: Si on vous frappe parce que vous avez fait le mal, et que vous le supportez, vous ne méritez aucun éloge pour cela.

ko.L: 여러분이 죄를 짓고 매를 맞으면서 참는다면, 무슨 칭찬이 [있겠습니까]?
ko.B: 잘못을 저질러서 매를 맞고 참는다면, 무슨 칭찬받을 일이 있겠습니까?
ko.R: 여러분이 잘못을 저질러서 매를 맞고 그것을 참는다면, 칭찬받을 일이 아닙니다.

vi.L: Vì có vinh dự gì, nếu khi phạm tội và bị đánh đòn, anh chị em chịu đựng?
vi.B: Vì có gì đáng khen khi anh chị em làm điều sai rồi chịu đựng đòn vọt?
vi.R: Nếu anh chị em bị đánh vì đã làm điều sai, và anh chị em chịu đựng, thì anh chị em chẳng đáng được khen gì cả.

pt.L: Pois que mérito [há] se, quando vocês pecam e são esbofeteados, suportam [isso]?
pt.B: Pois que mérito há em suportar pancadas quando vocês fizeram o mal?
pt.R: Se vocês apanham porque fizeram algo errado e aguentam isso, não merecem nenhum elogio.

decisions.choice: being struck: beaten with fists
decisions.reason: κολαφιζόμενοι means to hit with the fist. It is what was done to Jesus (Mark 14:65), and what slaves could expect from their owners.

decisions.choice: credit: praise or fame
decisions.reason: κλέος is fame or praise. A slave who endures a deserved beating earns nothing for it, before people or before God.

decisions.choice: you deserve no praise for that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: ἀλλ’ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε, τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: But if doing good and suffering you will endure, this [is] grace with God.

en.L: But if, when you do good and suffer, you endure [it], this [is] grace with God.
en.B: But if you do good and suffer for it and you endure, this finds favor with God.
en.R: But suppose you do what is right and you suffer for it. If you bear it patiently, God is pleased with you.

es.L: Pero si, cuando {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}}, lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, esto [es] gracia ante Dios.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}} por ello, y lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, esto halla favor ante Dios.
es.R: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo correcto y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}} por ello. Si lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}} con paciencia, Dios se agrada de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa, mkitenda mema na kuteswa, mtastahimili, hii [ni] neema mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini mkitenda mema na kuteswa kwa sababu hiyo, nanyi mkavumilia, hilo linapata kibali mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme mnatenda yaliyo mema, nanyi mnateswa kwa sababu hiyo. Mkivumilia kwa subira, Mungu anapendezwa nanyi.

fr.L: Mais si, quand vous faites le bien et souffrez, vous [le] supportez, c’est une grâce auprès de Dieu.
fr.B: Mais si vous faites le bien, que vous en souffrez et que vous tenez bon, cela trouve faveur auprès de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais imaginez que vous faites ce qui est juste et que vous en souffrez. Si vous le supportez avec patience, Dieu est content de vous.

ko.L: 그러나 여러분이 선을 행하다가 고난을 받으면서 참는다면, 이것은 하나님 앞에서 은혜입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 선을 행하다가 고난을 받고 그것을 참는다면, 그것은 하나님께서 기뻐하시는 일입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 여러분이 옳은 일을 하다가 고난을 받는다고 해 봅시다. 그때 여러분이 그것을 꾹 참는다면, 하나님께서 여러분을 기뻐하십니다.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu khi làm lành mà chịu khổ, anh chị em chịu đựng, thì đó [là] ân điển trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Nhưng nếu anh chị em làm điều lành mà phải chịu khổ, và anh chị em chịu đựng, thì điều đó được Đức Chúa Trời đẹp lòng.
vi.R: Nhưng giả sử anh chị em làm điều đúng mà phải chịu khổ vì điều đó. Nếu anh chị em kiên nhẫn chịu đựng, Đức Chúa Trời hài lòng về anh chị em.

pt.L: Mas se, quando fazem o bem e sofrem, vocês suportam [isso], isto [é] graça diante de Deus.
pt.B: Mas, se vocês fazem o bem, sofrem por isso e perseveram, isto conta com o favor de Deus.
pt.R: Mas imaginem que vocês fazem o que é certo e sofrem por isso. Se vocês suportarem com paciência, Deus se agrada de vocês.

decisions.choice: grace with God: what God approves
alternatives: a gift of grace from God
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, χάρις here is favor: patient endurance of suffering for doing good is what God looks on with approval.

decisions.choice: doing good and suffering, you endure: suffering because of the good one does
decisions.reason: ἀγαθοποιοῦντες and πάσχοντες stand side by side: those who do right and suffer for it (3:14, 3:17). ὑπομενεῖτε is to bear up, to stand firm under it.

decisions.choice: this finds favor with God (B); God is pleased with you (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, Balanced and Readable give the sense; Literal keeps "grace".

source.text: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε, ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: To this for you were called, because also Christ suffered for you, to you leaving an example so that you may follow the steps of him;

en.L: For to this you were called, because {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you may follow in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steps.
en.B: It was for this that God called you, because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} also suffered for you and left you a pattern to copy, so that you would walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footsteps.
en.R: God called you to this kind of life, because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} also suffered for you. He left you an example to copy, like a teacher who writes out letters for a child to trace. So follow where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} walked.

es.L: Porque para esto {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} llamados, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dejándo{{plural_you:les|os}} un modelo para que {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} de cerca {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} huellas.
es.B: Para esto Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} dejó un modelo que imitar, para que {{plural_you:caminen|caminéis}} siguiendo {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pasos.
es.R: Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a esta clase de vida, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él {{plural_you:les|os}} dejó un ejemplo para imitar, como un maestro que escribe letras para que un niño las calque. Así que {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} el camino por donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} anduvo.

sw.L: Kwa maana mliitwa kwa ajili ya hili, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu, akiwaachieni mfano wa kunakili ili mfuatilie alama za nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Ni kwa ajili ya hili Mungu aliwaita, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu, akawaachia mfano wa kunakili, ili mtembee katika nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Mungu aliwaita kwa maisha ya namna hii, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu. Aliwaachia mfano wa kuiga, kama mwalimu anayeandika herufi ili mtoto azifuatishe. Basi fuateni njia aliyopita {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

fr.L: Car c’est à cela que vous avez été appelés, parce que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aussi a souffert pour vous, vous laissant un modèle afin que vous suiviez {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} traces.
fr.B: C’est à cela que Dieu vous a appelés, car le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} aussi, a souffert pour vous et vous a laissé un modèle à reproduire, afin que vous marchiez sur {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} traces.
fr.R: Dieu vous a appelés à ce genre de vie, parce que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} aussi a souffert pour vous. Il vous a laissé un exemple à suivre, comme un maître qui écrit des lettres pour qu’un enfant les recopie en suivant le tracé. Alors suivez le chemin où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a marché.

ko.L: 여러분은 이것을 위하여 부르심을 받았습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서도 여러분을 위하여 고난을 받으시고, 여러분에게 본을 남기셔서 여러분이 그분의 발자취를 따르게 하셨기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 여러분을 부르신 것은 바로 이것을 위해서입니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서도 여러분을 위해 고난을 받으시고, 여러분에게 따라야 할 본을 남기셔서, 여러분이 그분의 발자취를 따라 걷게 하셨습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 여러분을 이런 삶으로 부르셨습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서도 여러분을 위해 고난을 받으셨기 때문입니다. 그분은 여러분에게 따라 할 본을 남기셨습니다. 선생님이 아이에게 글씨를 써 주고 그대로 따라 쓰게 하는 것과 같습니다. 그러니 그분이 걸어가신 길을 따라가십시오.

vi.L: Vì anh chị em đã được kêu gọi vào điều này, vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} cũng đã chịu khổ vì anh chị em, để lại cho anh chị em một gương mẫu, để anh chị em theo dấu chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Chính vì điều này mà Đức Chúa Trời đã kêu gọi anh chị em, vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} cũng đã chịu khổ vì anh chị em, và để lại cho anh chị em một khuôn mẫu để noi theo, hầu cho anh chị em bước theo dấu chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã kêu gọi anh chị em sống như vậy, vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} cũng đã chịu khổ vì anh chị em. Ngài để lại cho anh chị em một gương mẫu để làm theo, như thầy giáo viết sẵn những con chữ cho học trò tô theo. Vậy hãy bước theo con đường {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đi.

pt.L: Pois para isto vocês foram chamados, porque também {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} sofreu por vocês, deixando-lhes um exemplo para que sigam os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} passos.
pt.B: Foi para isso que Deus chamou vocês, porque {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} também sofreu por vocês e lhes deixou um modelo a ser copiado, para que vocês andem nas {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} pegadas.
pt.R: Deus chamou vocês para esse tipo de vida, porque {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} também sofreu por vocês. Ele deixou um exemplo para vocês copiarem, como um professor que escreve as letras para uma criança cobrir. Então sigam pelo caminho por onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} andou.

decisions.choice: to this you were called: to doing good and suffering patiently
decisions.reason: τοῦτο points back to verse 20. God, who called them (verse 9; 1:15), called them to a life that may include unjust suffering, as Christ's did.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "suffered"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "died" instead of ἔπαθεν ("suffered"); the same variation occurs at 3:18. "Suffered" fits the subject of these verses, which is suffering. Some manuscripts also have "for us ... leaving us" instead of "for you ... leaving you". Reviewers must check both against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an example: a pattern to copy
decisions.reason: ὑπογραμμὸν was the model of letters a child traced over when learning to write. Christ's way of suffering is the pattern believers write over.

decisions.choice: for you: on your behalf
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ means for someone's benefit. Christ's suffering was an example, but more than an example: it was for them, as verse 24 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: follow in his steps: walk where he walked
decisions.reason: ἴχνεσιν are footprints. To follow them is to go the way he went.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God called you
decisions.reason: The one who calls in 1 Peter is God (m1); Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: like a teacher who writes out letters for a child to trace
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture in the word (m3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish puts the article before "Mesías" but not before "Cristo", so the span takes it in.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}
decisions.reason: The English Literal's bare "Messiah" would read "Messias sofreu" without an article, which Portuguese does not say; the article goes inside the alternative, as at Balanced.

source.text: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: who sin not did nor was found deceit in the mouth of him;

en.L: He did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.B: He never sinned, and no one ever found deceit in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.R: He never sinned. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never lied or tried to deceive anyone.

es.L: Él no cometió pecado, ni se halló engaño en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.B: Nunca pecó, y nadie encontró jamás engaño en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.R: Nunca pecó. Y nunca mintió ni trató de engañar a nadie.

sw.L: Hakufanya dhambi, wala udanganyifu haukupatikana katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.B: Hakutenda dhambi kamwe, na hakuna mtu aliyekuta udanganyifu katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.R: Hakutenda dhambi hata kidogo. Wala hakusema uongo, wala hakujaribu kumdanganya mtu yeyote.

fr.L: Il n’a pas commis de péché, et il ne s’est pas trouvé de ruse dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche.
fr.B: Il n’a jamais péché, et personne n’a jamais trouvé de mensonge dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche.
fr.R: Il n’a jamais péché. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a jamais menti ni cherché à tromper personne.

ko.L: 그분은 죄를 짓지 않으셨고, 그분의 입에서는 거짓도 발견되지 않았습니다.
ko.B: 그분은 한 번도 죄를 짓지 않으셨고, 그분의 입에서는 아무도 거짓을 찾지 못했습니다.
ko.R: 그분은 한 번도 죄를 짓지 않으셨습니다. 그리고 한 번도 거짓말을 하시거나 누구를 속이려고 하지 않으셨습니다.

vi.L: Ngài đã không phạm tội, cũng không tìm thấy sự dối trá trong miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài chưa hề phạm tội, và không ai tìm thấy sự dối trá trong miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngài không bao giờ phạm tội. Ngài cũng không bao giờ nói dối hay tìm cách lừa gạt ai.

pt.L: Ele não cometeu pecado, nem foi achado engano na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca.
pt.B: Ele nunca pecou, e ninguém jamais encontrou engano na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca.
pt.R: Ele nunca pecou. E nunca mentiu nem tentou enganar ninguém.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:9, about the suffering servant of the Lord
decisions.reason: Isaiah 52:13-53:12 describes the servant of the Lord who suffers for the sins of others. Peter uses its words in verses 22-25 to describe Jesus. Verse 22 follows the Greek of Isaiah 53:9 closely, with "sin" where that translation has "lawlessness".

decisions.choice: who: Christ (verse 21)
decisions.reason: ὃς begins the first of three statements about Christ (verses 22, 23, 24). The SBLGNT punctuation makes each its own sentence.

decisions.choice: deceit: lies and trickery
decisions.reason: δόλος is the same word as in verse 1. Christ is the pattern of what the readers are to put away.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun for Christ. A sentence starting with "He" has no span.

decisions.choice: the words of Isaiah 53 woven into Peter's sentence in the letter's 합쇼체, with the honorific for Christ
decisions.reason: Here Peter does not quote with a formula but tells of Christ in the words of Isaiah 53 (meaning decisions), so the sentence stays in the letter's 합쇼체 and gives Christ the honorific, through verse 25.

source.text: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει, παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως·

records.literal_gloss: who being reviled not reviled in return, suffering not threatened, kept handing over however to the [one] judging justly;

en.L: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reviled, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not revile in return; when suffering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not threaten, but kept handing [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}] over to the one who judges justly.
en.B: People heaped abuse on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer abuse with abuse. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made no threats, but went on handing {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over to the God who judges justly.
en.R: When people insulted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not insult them back. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not threaten to pay them back. Instead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept putting {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} into the hands of God, who always judges fairly.

es.L: Siendo injuriado, no injuriaba a su vez; padeciendo, no amenazaba, sino que se iba entregando al que juzga justamente.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cubrían de insultos, no respondía con insultos. Mientras sufría, no profería amenazas, sino que seguía poniéndose en manos del Dios que juzga con justicia.
es.R: Cuando la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} insultaba, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no les devolvía el insulto. Cuando sufría, no amenazaba con vengarse. Al contrario, seguía poniéndose en manos de Dios, que siempre juzga con justicia.

sw.L: Akitukanwa, hakujibu kwa matusi; akiteswa, hakutisha, bali aliendelea kujikabidhi kwa yule anayehukumu kwa haki.
sw.B: Watu walipomtukana, hakujibu matusi kwa matusi. Alipoteswa, hakutoa vitisho, bali aliendelea kujikabidhi kwa Mungu anayehukumu kwa haki.
sw.R: Watu walipomtukana, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuwatukana tena. Alipoteswa, hakutishia kulipiza kisasi. Badala yake, aliendelea kujiweka mikononi mwa Mungu, ambaye daima huhukumu kwa haki.

fr.L: Insulté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne rendait pas l’insulte ; souffrant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne menaçait pas, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} remettait [{{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} cause] à celui qui juge justement.
fr.B: On {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accablait d’insultes, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne répondait pas à l’insulte par l’insulte. Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffrait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne proférait pas de menaces, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} continuait à remettre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} cause entre les mains du Dieu qui juge avec justice.
fr.R: Quand les gens {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}insultaient, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne leur rendait pas leurs insultes. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffrait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne les menaçait pas de vengeance. Au contraire, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} confiait toujours {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie à Dieu, qui juge toujours avec justice.

ko.L: 그분은 모욕을 당하셔도 맞서 모욕하지 않으셨고, 고난을 받으셔도 위협하지 않으시고, 공정하게 심판하시는 분께 [자신을] 계속 맡기셨습니다.
ko.B: 사람들이 그분께 온갖 모욕을 퍼부었지만, 그분은 모욕으로 갚지 않으셨습니다. 고난을 받으시면서도 위협하지 않으시고, 공정하게 심판하시는 하나님께 자신을 맡기셨습니다.
ko.R: 사람들이 그분을 모욕했을 때, 그분은 똑같이 모욕하지 않으셨습니다. 고난을 받으셨을 때도 갚아 주겠다고 위협하지 않으셨습니다. 그 대신 언제나 공정하게 심판하시는 하나님의 손에 자신을 맡기셨습니다.

vi.L: Khi bị nhục mạ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nhục mạ lại; khi chịu khổ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không hăm dọa, nhưng cứ phó thác [chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] cho Đấng xét xử công minh.
vi.B: Người ta sỉ nhục {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không lấy sỉ nhục đáp lại. Khi chịu khổ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không hăm dọa ai, nhưng cứ phó thác chính mình cho Đức Chúa Trời, là Đấng xét xử công minh.
vi.R: Khi người ta lăng mạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không lăng mạ lại. Khi chịu khổ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không dọa sẽ trả thù. Thay vào đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứ giao phó chính mình trong tay Đức Chúa Trời, là Đấng luôn xét xử công bằng.

pt.L: Quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era insultado, não insultava em resposta; quando sofria, não ameaçava, mas [se] entregava àquele que julga com justiça.
pt.B: As pessoas {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} cobriam de insultos, mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não respondia insulto com insulto. Enquanto sofria, não fazia ameaças, mas continuava a se entregar ao Deus que julga com justiça.
pt.R: Quando as pessoas {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} insultavam, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não insultava de volta. Quando sofria, não ameaçava se vingar. Em vez disso, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} continuava se colocando nas mãos de Deus, que sempre julga com justiça.

decisions.choice: when insulted, when suffering: what he kept doing throughout his suffering
decisions.reason: ἀντελοιδόρει, ἠπείλει and παρεδίδου are imperfects: they describe how he acted again and again through his trial and death (Mark 14:61; 15:5). The verse echoes Isaiah 53:7.

decisions.choice: handed over: entrusted himself (and his cause) to God
alternatives: handed over those who wronged him
decisions.reason: παρεδίδου has no object in the Greek. The most likely object is himself, with his case, left in God's hands (compare 4:19, where believers entrust their souls to God). Some read it as handing over those who wronged him for God to judge. The point is the same either way: he left judgment to God and did not take revenge.

decisions.choice: the one who judges justly: God
decisions.reason: κρίνοντι is God, who judges each person's work without favoritism (1:17; 4:5).

decisions.choice: [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object the verb needs (m2).

decisions.choice: the God who judges justly (B); God, who always judges fairly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the judge (m3).

decisions.choice: se iba entregando (L); poniéndose (B, R)
decisions.reason: The reflexive "se" supplies the object the Greek verb lacks (meaning decision: he entrusted himself), so Spanish needs no bracket. Being part of the verb, it takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: kujikabidhi (L, B); kujiweka (R)
decisions.reason: The reflexive "-ji-" in the verb supplies the object the Greek lacks (meaning decision: he entrusted himself), so Swahili needs no bracket.

decisions.choice: remettait [sa cause] (L); remettre sa cause (B); confiait sa vie (R)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the meaning decision reads it as Jesus entrusting himself and his cause to God. French would say "se remettre", but a reflexive pronoun for Christ has no deity_pronoun form in the style guide, so French names what he handed over.

decisions.choice: "chính mình" (B, R) for himself, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese says "oneself" with the reflexive "mình", which has no capital form, as the Vietnamese John does (10:11). Literal brackets the supplied object with the span, as the English brackets "himself".

source.text: ὃς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἀπογενόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν· οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε.

records.literal_gloss: who the sins of us himself carried up in the body of him onto the tree, so that to the sins having died to the righteousness we may live; of whom by the bruise you were healed.

en.L: He {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} carried up our sins in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body onto the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness; by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} bruise you were healed.
en.B: He {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} carried our sins in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body up onto the cross, so that we would be done with sins and live for righteousness. By the bruises {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bore you have been healed.
en.R: Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} carried our sins in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body on the cross. He did this so that we would be finished with sin and would live the righteous life God wants. You have been healed because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was beaten and wounded.

es.L: Él mismo cargó nuestros pecados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo sobre el madero, para que, muertos a los pecados, vivamos para la justicia; por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} herida {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} sanados.
es.B: Él mismo cargó nuestros pecados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio cuerpo hasta la cruz, para que acabemos con los pecados y vivamos para la justicia. Por los golpes que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recibió, {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} sido sanados.
es.R: Jesús mismo cargó nuestros pecados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo en la cruz. Lo hizo para que termináramos con el pecado y viviéramos la vida justa que Dios quiere. {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotros habéis}} sido sanados porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fue golpeado y herido.

sw.L: Yeye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alizibeba dhambi zetu katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hadi juu ya mti, ili, tukiwa tumekufa kwa dhambi, tuishi kwa haki; kwa jeraha {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} mliponywa.
sw.B: Yeye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alizibeba dhambi zetu katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe hadi msalabani, ili tuachane na dhambi na tuishi kwa ajili ya haki. Kwa majeraha aliyoyapata ninyi mmeponywa.
sw.R: Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alizibeba dhambi zetu katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} msalabani. Alifanya hivyo ili tuachane kabisa na dhambi na tuishi maisha ya haki ambayo Mungu anayataka. Mmeponywa kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipigwa na kujeruhiwa.

fr.L: Lui-même a porté nos péchés dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps jusque sur le bois, afin que, morts aux péchés, nous vivions pour la justice ; par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} meurtrissure vous avez été guéris.
fr.B: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} qui a porté nos péchés dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre corps jusque sur la croix, afin que nous en ayons fini avec les péchés et que nous vivions pour la justice. Par les meurtrissures qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a subies, vous avez été guéris.
fr.R: Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} a porté nos péchés dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps sur la croix. Il l’a fait pour que nous en ayons fini avec le péché et que nous vivions la vie juste que Dieu veut. Vous avez été guéris parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été frappé et blessé.

ko.L: 그분은 친히 나무 위에서 그분의 몸으로 우리의 죄를 지셨습니다. 이는 우리가 죄에 대하여 죽고 의에 대하여 살게 하려는 것입니다. 그분이 맞으신 상처로 여러분은 나음을 얻었습니다.
ko.B: 그분은 우리의 죄를 친히 그분의 몸에 지시고 십자가에 달리셨습니다. 그것은 우리가 죄와 끝을 맺고 의를 위해 살게 하시려는 것입니다. 그분이 맞으신 상처로 여러분은 나았습니다.
ko.R: 예수님께서는 친히 우리의 죄를 그분의 몸에 지시고 십자가에 달리셨습니다. 그렇게 하신 것은 우리가 죄와 완전히 끝내고, 하나님께서 원하시는 의로운 삶을 살게 하시려는 것입니다. 그분이 맞으시고 상처를 입으셨기 때문에 여러분은 나았습니다.

vi.L: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã mang tội lỗi chúng ta trong thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên cây gỗ, để chúng ta, đã chết đối với tội lỗi, được sống cho sự công chính; bởi lằn roi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà anh chị em đã được chữa lành.
vi.B: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gánh tội lỗi chúng ta trong thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên thập tự giá, để chúng ta dứt khỏi tội lỗi và sống cho sự công chính. Bởi những lằn roi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chịu mà anh chị em đã được chữa lành.
vi.R: Chính Đức Giê-xu đã gánh tội lỗi chúng ta trong thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên thập tự giá. Ngài làm vậy để chúng ta dứt khỏi tội lỗi và sống đời sống công chính mà Đức Chúa Trời muốn. Anh chị em đã được chữa lành vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã bị đánh đập và bị thương tích.

pt.L: Ele mesmo levou os nossos pecados no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} corpo sobre o madeiro, para que, tendo morrido para os pecados, vivamos para a justiça; pelo {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} vergão vocês foram curados.
pt.B: Ele mesmo carregou os nossos pecados no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio corpo até a cruz, para que acabássemos com os pecados e vivêssemos para a justiça. Pelas marcas das pancadas que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} levou, vocês foram curados.
pt.R: O próprio Jesus carregou os nossos pecados no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} corpo, na cruz. Ele fez isso para que nós acabássemos com o pecado e vivêssemos a vida justa que Deus quer. Vocês foram curados porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi espancado e ferido.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:4, 53:11-12: the servant bears the sins of many
decisions.reason: ἀνήνεγκεν is the verb of Isaiah 53:12 in the Greek Old Testament, "he bore the sins of many". It is also the verb for offering a sacrifice on the altar (2:5). Christ carried our sins up onto the cross as a sacrifice.

decisions.choice: the tree: the cross
decisions.reason: ξύλον means wood, and was used for the cross (Acts 5:30; 10:39). It recalls Deuteronomy 21:23, where one hanged on a tree is under God's curse (Galatians 3:13).

decisions.choice: having died to sins: being finished with sin
decisions.reason: ἀπογενόμενοι means to be away from something, and was used of dying. With ἁμαρτίαις it means that believers have broken with sin: they are done with it, so that they may live for what is right (compare Romans 6:2, 6:11).

decisions.choice: righteousness: right living before God
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνῃ here is the righteousness of life that God requires, set against the sins just named (compare 3:14).

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:5: by his bruise we are healed
decisions.reason: μώλωπι is the welt or bruise left by a beating, the word in Isaiah 53:5. Writing to slaves who could be beaten (verse 20), Peter says that Christ's beating has healed them. Isaiah has "we"; Peter changes it to "you".

decisions.choice: our sins, we might live, you were healed
decisions.reason: Peter includes himself ("our sins", "we") and then turns back to his readers ("you"), continuing the address to slaves in verses 18-20.

decisions.choice: the cross
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the tree was (m2); Literal keeps "tree".

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names him.

decisions.choice: bruises (B); was beaten and wounded (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a mark from a beating (m5); Balanced and Readable keep that picture.

decisions.choice: Él mismo; Jesús mismo, no span
decisions.reason: Where the English marks "himself", Spanish has "mismo" after a pronoun or name at the start of the sentence. "Mismo" is not a pronoun and "Él" is capitalised there anyway, so there is no span.

decisions.choice: le bois (L); la croix (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means wood or a tree and here names the cross (meaning decision m2). French "le bois" is the traditional word for the cross in this sense; "l’arbre" would make readers think of a living tree.

decisions.choice: "나무" (L); "십자가" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The tree is the cross (meaning decision); Literal keeps "나무", the word of Deuteronomy 21:23 behind it, and Balanced and Readable say "십자가".

decisions.choice: "cây gỗ" (L); "thập tự giá" (B, R) for the tree
decisions.reason: Peter calls the cross a tree (m2), as Deuteronomy 21:23 speaks of one hanged on a tree; Literal keeps his word, and Balanced and Readable name the cross, as the English does.

decisions.choice: o madeiro (L); vergão (L); as marcas das pancadas (B)
decisions.reason: "Madeiro" is the Portuguese word for the wooden beam and has long been used for the cross. For the mark of a beating (m5), Literal says "vergão", the welt a blow leaves; Balanced says "as marcas das pancadas", tying it to the beatings of 2:20. "Pisaduras" is old Bible language, and "feridas" loses the beating. "Ele mesmo" and "O próprio Jesus" take no span: style section 7 gives the setting to pronouns, and "mesmo" after a sentence-initial "Ele" is written plainly.

source.text: ἦτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα πλανώμενοι, ἀλλὰ ἐπεστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: You were for like sheep going astray, but you turned now to the shepherd and overseer of the souls of you.

en.L: For you were like sheep going astray, but now you have turned back to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
en.B: For you used to wander like lost sheep, but now you have come back to the shepherd who watches over your souls.
en.R: You were like sheep that had wandered away. But now you have come back to Jesus, who is your Shepherd. He watches over you and cares for your lives.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:andaban|andabais}} extraviados como ovejas, pero ahora {{plural_you:se han vuelto|os habéis vuelto}} al Pastor y Guardián de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.B: Porque {{plural_you:andaban|andabais}} errantes como ovejas perdidas, pero ahora {{plural_you:han|habéis}} vuelto al Pastor que cuida de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes eran|Vosotros erais}} como ovejas que se habían alejado. Pero ahora {{plural_you:han|habéis}} vuelto a Jesús, que es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Pastor. Él {{plural_you:los|os}} vigila y cuida de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} vidas.

sw.L: Kwa maana mlikuwa kama kondoo wanaotangatanga, lakini sasa mmerudi kwa Mchungaji na Mlinzi wa nafsi zenu.
sw.B: Kwa maana mlikuwa mkitangatanga kama kondoo waliopotea, lakini sasa mmemrudia Mchungaji anayezilinda nafsi zenu.
sw.R: Mlikuwa kama kondoo waliopotea njia. Lakini sasa mmemrudia Yesu, aliye Mchungaji wenu. Yeye huwalinda na kuyatunza maisha yenu.

fr.L: Car vous étiez comme des brebis errantes, mais vous êtes maintenant retournés vers le berger et gardien de vos âmes.
fr.B: Car vous étiez autrefois comme des brebis égarées, mais maintenant vous êtes revenus au berger qui veille sur vos âmes.
fr.R: Vous étiez comme des brebis qui s’étaient perdues. Mais maintenant, vous êtes revenus vers Jésus, votre Berger. Il veille sur vous et prend soin de votre vie.

ko.L: 여러분은 길을 잃고 헤매는 양들과 같았으나, 이제는 여러분의 영혼의 목자이시며 감독자이신 분께로 돌아왔습니다.
ko.B: 여러분은 길 잃은 양처럼 헤매고 있었지만, 이제는 여러분의 영혼을 지켜보시는 목자께로 돌아왔습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 길을 잃고 헤매는 양과 같았습니다. 그러나 이제 여러분은 여러분의 목자이신 예수님께 돌아왔습니다. 그분은 여러분을 지켜보시고 여러분의 생명을 돌보십니다.

vi.L: Vì anh chị em giống như chiên đi lạc, nhưng nay anh chị em đã trở về cùng Đấng Chăn Giữ và Giám Mục của linh hồn anh chị em.
vi.B: Vì trước kia anh chị em đi lang thang như chiên lạc, nhưng nay anh chị em đã trở về với Đấng Chăn Giữ, là Đấng coi sóc linh hồn anh chị em.
vi.R: Anh chị em giống như những con chiên đã đi lạc. Nhưng bây giờ anh chị em đã trở về với Đức Giê-xu, là Đấng Chăn Giữ của anh chị em. Ngài trông nom anh chị em và chăm sóc đời sống anh chị em.

pt.L: Pois vocês eram como ovelhas desgarradas, mas agora voltaram para o pastor e supervisor das almas de vocês.
pt.B: Pois vocês andavam perdidos como ovelhas desgarradas, mas agora voltaram para o pastor que cuida das almas de vocês.
pt.R: Vocês eram como ovelhas que tinham se perdido. Mas agora voltaram para Jesus, que é o Pastor de vocês. Ele vigia vocês e cuida da vida de vocês.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:6: all we like sheep have gone astray
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:6 confesses that all of us have wandered like sheep. Peter applies it to his readers' life before they turned to Christ.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "going astray" agreeing with "you"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a form of the participle that agrees with πρόβατα ("sheep") rather than with "you" (πλανώμενοι). The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: you turned back: you returned
decisions.reason: ἐπεστράφητε is used for turning to God in repentance (Acts 3:19). Its passive form here has the sense "you turned", and it may also suggest that they were brought back.

decisions.choice: the shepherd and overseer: Christ, as God is Israel's shepherd
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 34 and Psalm 23 the Lord is the shepherd of his people. Here Christ is the ποιμένα, as in 5:4 he is the chief shepherd. ἐπίσκοπον is one who watches over and cares for others; the same pair of words is used for church leaders in 5:2.

decisions.choice: the shepherd who watches over your souls (B); He watches over you and cares for your lives (R)
decisions.reason: "Overseer" sounds like a supervisor, and "bishop" names a later church office. Balanced and Readable say what the overseer does. Literal keeps "overseer".

decisions.choice: Jesus, who is your Shepherd
decisions.reason: Readable names the shepherd (m4).

decisions.choice: Pastor y Guardián
decisions.reason: "Obispo" names a later church office and "supervisor" sounds like a workplace; "Guardián" is one who watches over others, as the meaning decision says. The same pair of words is kept for this title in the letter.

decisions.choice: Mchungaji na Mlinzi
decisions.reason: "Askofu" names a later church office; "Mlinzi" is one who watches over and protects others, as the meaning decision says. The same pair of words is kept for this title in the letter.

decisions.choice: le berger et gardien (L); le berger qui veille sur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews, "berger" keeps the picture of the shepherd; "pasteur" now first means a minister. The second word is the one later used for a bishop, but here it means one who watches over, and "gardien" says that.

decisions.choice: "목자이시며 감독자이신 분" (L); "영혼을 지켜보시는 목자" (B); "목자이신 예수님 ... 지켜보시고 ... 돌보십니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The overseer is one who watches over others (meaning decision); "감독" now suggests a film director or a sports manager, so Literal says "감독자" and Balanced and Readable say what he does.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Chăn Giữ" for the Shepherd; "Giám Mục" (L), "Đấng coi sóc" (B), "trông nom" (R) for the overseer
decisions.reason: Christ is the shepherd and overseer, as God is Israel's shepherd (m4), so both are titles with "Đấng". "Giám mục" is the literal word for overseer, but it now names a church office, so only Literal keeps it, capitalised as a title of Christ; Balanced and Readable say what he does.

decisions.choice: supervisor
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "supervisor", the style guide's word for this title, so that the reader can see the same pair of words used for church leaders in 5:2 (m4). "Bispo" names a later church office.
